steps.question: Which states get their own visible value?

steps.rule: The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surfaces it sits on: darker in light, and darker in dark too, as raised layers take the lighter step.
steps.pick: neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.
steps.darkPick: neutral.0: We use a step darker than content for the item under the pointer or the keyboard in dark, in order to mark it as a band on both surfaces it meets: 1.13:1 on surface.default and 1.38:1 on surface.raised. The fill does this by stepping darker, as raised layers took the lighter step; muted text still reads 7.88:1 on it. So the hovered row or menu item shows on cards and menus alike, because hover and focus have their own look (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).

steps.question: What rises above the page?
steps.why: Cards lift slightly to group offers.
The shadow shows a menu or dialog floats above the page. Without it, it blends into the cards.

steps.rule: Fills that float above content. In dark, one step lighter than content, so height reads by tone.
steps.pick: neutral.0, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge and its one shadow, not by its fill.
steps.darkPick: neutral.100: We use one step lighter than content for menus, dialogs and raised cards in dark, in order to show height by tone, 1.22:1 on surface.default. The lighter fill does this by the dark-mode depth rule: the higher a layer sits, the lighter its surface. So customers see a menu above the page even where its shadow barely shows, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).

steps.rule: Quiet edges and dividers. Decorative, so it has no contrast minimum.
steps.pick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.18:1, on surface.canvas). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.
steps.darkPick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.41:1, on surface.raised). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.

steps.pick: radius.8: We use an 8px corner for Aster's cards and dialogs in order to make each card read as a separate object, in a calm tone by brand convention. A modest radius does this by breaking the outline with a curve twice the 4px control corner. So a plan card reads as one object without feeling soft, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and each brand colors a neutral base (brand.q1).

shadow.overlay: We use step 2 of the shadow scale for menus and dialogs in order to show floating height, one step above the cards. The cast shade does this by a 12px offset and a 32px blur at 16%, four times the card's blur. So a menu floats clear above the cards in every brand, because cards and overlays rise (elevation.roles) and shadows are soft (elevation.values).
steps.darkPick: shadow.overlay-dark: We use the light overlay shadow's shape in dark in order to show the same floating height by the dark-shade relation. The cast shade does this by the same 12px offset and 32px blur, at 50% black instead of 16%. So a menu still floats above the cards, though its shade reads weaker on dark than in light, because cards and overlays rise (elevation.roles) and dark ships for every brand (theming.values).

radius.4: We use a 4px corner for Aster's menu options in order to keep nesting by the relation: the 8px surface corner minus the panel's 4px padding. The inner radius does this by following the outer curve at the padding's distance. So an option's curve runs parallel to its menu's curve, because Aster's surfaces take 8px (shape.roles, brand.q1) and the panel's padding is 4px (spacing.values).
